objectives.en: Show that a simple pendulum performs SHM for small angles

narration.en: Galileo timed a swinging lamp in a cathedral with his pulse. Big swings or small, each took the same time. Why?
narration.kn: ಗೆಲಿಲಿಯೋ ಚರ್ಚ್‌ನಲ್ಲಿ ತೂಗುತ್ತಿದ್ದ ದೀಪದ ಸಮಯವನ್ನು ತನ್ನ ನಾಡಿಯಿಂದ ಅಳೆದನು. ದೊಡ್ಡ ಅಥವಾ ಸಣ್ಣ ತೂಗಾಟ, ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದಕ್ಕೂ ಅದೇ ಸಮಯ. ಏಕೆ?

title.en: Why a pendulum is simple harmonic

body.en: A bob of mass m on a light string of length L, displaced by angle θ, feels a restoring torque τ = −mgL sin θ. For small angles sin θ ≈ θ (in radians), so τ ≈ −mgLθ: the angular acceleration is proportional to θ and opposite to it, which is SHM with ω = √(g/L).
body.kn: θ ಕೋನದಷ್ಟು ಸರಿಸಿದ ಲೋಲಕದ ಮೇಲೆ ಪುನಃಸ್ಥಾಪಕ ಟಾರ್ಕ್ τ = −mgL sin θ. ಸಣ್ಣ ಕೋನಕ್ಕೆ sin θ ≈ θ, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಇದು ω = √(g/L) ಇರುವ ಸ.ಸಂ.ಚ.

points.en: Small angles only: sin θ ≈ θ

narration.en: A bob of mass m on a light string of length L, displaced by angle θ, feels a restoring torque τ = −mgL sin θ. For small angles sin θ ≈ θ (in radians), so τ ≈ −mgLθ: the angular acceleration is proportional to θ and opposite to it, which is SHM with ω = √(g/L).
narration.kn: θ ಕೋನದಷ್ಟು ಸರಿಸಿದ ಲೋಲಕದ ಮೇಲೆ ಪುನಃಸ್ಥಾಪಕ ಟಾರ್ಕ್ τ = −mgL sin θ. ಸಣ್ಣ ಕೋನಕ್ಕೆ sin θ ≈ θ, ಆದ್ದರಿಂದ ಇದು ω = √(g/L) ಇರುವ ಸ.ಸಂ.ಚ.

body.en: The period is T = 2π√(L/g). It does not depend on the mass of the bob, nor on the amplitude as long as it is small. A seconds pendulum has a period of 2 s; its length is about 0.99 m on Earth. Measuring T for a known L gives g = 4π²L/T².
body.kn: ಆವರ್ತಕಾಲ T = 2π√(L/g). ಇದು ಗುಂಡಿನ ದ್ರವ್ಯರಾಶಿ ಮತ್ತು ಸಣ್ಣ ಕಂಪನ ವಿಸ್ತಾರವನ್ನು ಅವಲಂಬಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. ಸೆಕೆಂಡ್ ಲೋಲಕದ ಆವರ್ತಕಾಲ 2 s, ಉದ್ದ ಸುಮಾರು 0.99 m.

points.en: T independent of mass and small amplitude
Seconds pendulum: T = 2 s, L ≈ 0.99 m

narration.en: The period is T = 2π√(L/g). It does not depend on the mass of the bob, nor on the amplitude as long as it is small. A seconds pendulum has a period of 2 s; its length is about 0.99 m on Earth. Measuring T for a known L gives g = 4π²L/T².

problem.en: Find the length of a seconds pendulum (T = 2 s) where g = 9.8 m s⁻².

narration.en: Let us solve this together. Find the length of a seconds pendulum (T = 2 s) where g = 9.8 m s⁻².

body.en: T ∝ √L and T ∝ 1/√g. Four times the length doubles the period; a planet with four times the gravity halves it.

narration.en: Square root rules. T ∝ √L and T ∝ 1/√g. Four times the length doubles the period; a planet with four times the gravity halves it.
